correctness.rationale: The five Walsh eigenspaces have dimensions 1,4,6,4,1, giving the sharp six-input lower bound. For any six chosen antipodal representatives, the 6x6 middle-eigenspace restriction is invertible iff a 2x2 Jacobi complementary minor of the 8x8 even Walsh table is invertible, exactly when the two omitted antipodal classes have opposite parity. Every nonzero degree-one Walsh combination vanishes on at most four antipodal classes; degree-three rows are a parity twist and outer degrees are nowhere zero. Thus all PBH modes pass precisely under the stated rule. The 1024 count is exact. The 8 orbits are exhaustively checked over all 384 graph automorphisms by verify.py, which separately verifies all 8008 six-subsets using exact GF(257) ranks; Hadamard bound 216<257 guarantees rational equivalence. The proof is finite and complete for Q4.

value.rationale: The four-dimensional Boolean cube is a canonical symmetry-rich network, with a six-dimensional repeated eigenspace forcing at least six independently controlled coordinates. The exact structure shows why only 1024 of 8008 minimum-size placements actually work and gives a constant-time geometric selection rule rather than determinant testing. Classifying eight symmetry-inequivalent layouts is directly useful for exhaustive optimal sensor/actuator placement and as a benchmark for structural network-control methods. It is a motivated complete classification, not an arbitrary invariant computation or a trivial lower-bound restatement.
